headings: Chronic Cough in Patients with Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis and Non-IPF Interstitial Lung Diseases
Exclusive License Agreement with Keenova Therapeutics plc
Approval and Regulation of Drugs in the U.S.
paragraphs: We are a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the development and commercialization of the investigational therapy Haduvio (oral nalbuphine ER) for the treatment of chronic cough in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, or IPF, non-IPF interstitial lung disease, or non-IPF ILD, and refractory chronic cough, or RCC.

Haduvio is an oral extended-release formulation of nalbuphine. Haduvio acts on the cough reflex arc both centrally and peripherally as a kappa receptor agonist and a mu receptor antagonist ("KAMA"), targeting opioid receptors that play a key role in controlling chronic cough. The kappa- and mu-opioid receptors are known to be critical mediators of cough. Nalbuphine has been approved and marketed as an injectable for pain indications for decades in the United States, or the U.S., and Europe. Nalbuphine's mechanism of action also mitigates the risk of abuse associated with mu-opioid agonists because it antagonizes, or blocks, the mu-opioid receptor. Parenteral nalbuphine is not scheduled as a controlled substance by the U.S. Drug Enforcement Agency and in most of Europe. We believe this makes Haduvio a promising potential therapy for the treatment of chronic cough in patients with IPF, non-IPF ILD, and RCC.

IPF-related Chronic Cough Program. We are developing Haduvio for the treatment of IPF-related chronic cough, which is a progressive fibrosing interstitial lung disease associated with high mortality rates. After an IPF diagnosis, the median survival is 3 to 5 years, during which time patients suffer from chronic cough, dyspnea, and fatigue. IPF-related chronic cough is a condition with high unmet need and no therapies approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, or FDA. There are approximately 150,000 U.S. patients with IPF, and two-thirds of these patients have uncontrolled chronic cough. The impact of chronic cough is significant, with patients coughing up to 1,500 times per day. This consistent cough, and any associated damage, may lead to a higher risk of morbidity and mortality, including worsening disease, a higher risk of progression, increased respiratory hospitalizations, and a decline in patients' physical, psychological, and social quality of life.

In June 2025, we announced positive topline results from our Phase 2b CORAL trial, which was a dose-ranging study evaluating the efficacy, safety and tolerability of Haduvio for IPF-related chronic cough. The Phase 2b CORAL trial was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-arm design that evaluated three different dose groups of Haduvio (108 mg BID, 54 mg BID and 27 mg BID) as compared to placebo. The primary efficacy endpoint for the trial was the relative change in 24-hour cough frequency (coughs per hour) for the modified intent-to-treat, or mITT, population at the end of Week 6 versus Baseline for Haduvio compared to placebo, as measured via an objective cough monitor. The mITT population consists of all randomized patients who received at least one dose of study drug or placebo (n=165). The primary efficacy endpoint in the Phase 2b CORAL trial was achieved, demonstrating statistically significant reductions in 24-hour cough frequency across all dose groups at Week 6. The 108 mg BID, 54 mg BID and 27 mg BID dose groups achieved statistically significant reductions from Baseline of 60.2% (p<0.0001), 53.4% (p<0.0001), and 47.9% (p<0.01), respectively, compared to a placebo reduction from Baseline of 16.9%.

We have completed an End-of-Phase 2 meeting with the FDA. At the meeting, we gained overall alignment on the plan for the remaining clinical studies to potentially support an NDA submission for nalbuphine ER, including two pivotal Phase 3 clinical trials and agreement on the remaining Phase 1 clinical studies. The Phase 3 trials will run in parallel, and we remain on track to initiate the first Phase 3 trial in the second quarter of 2026 and the second Phase 3 trial in the second half of 2026. The first of the two Phase 3 trials is planned to enroll approximately 300 patients and have 52 weeks of fixed dosing with nalbuphine ER 54 mg twice-a-day (BID), with the primary endpoint at 24 weeks of fixed dosing. The second Phase 3 trial is planned to enroll approximately 130 patients with and have 12 weeks of fixed dosing with nalbuphine ER 54 mg BID. The primary efficacy endpoint for both trials will be the relative change from Baseline in 24-hour cough frequency (coughs per hour), as determined by an objective cough monitor, for nalbuphine ER compared with placebo. These trial designs are subject to final review of the protocols by the FDA.

Non-IPF ILD-related Chronic Cough Program. We also plan to develop Haduvio for the treatment of non-IPF ILD-related chronic cough. Many patients diagnosed with non-IPF ILD suffer from a dry, non-productive chronic cough that is as disruptive as the cough associated with IPF. Cough may be an independent predictor of disease progression in non-IPF ILDs, and therefore we believe chronic cough may contribute to the progression of the underlying disease and worsening health outcomes.

Approximately 228,000 adults in the U.S. and greater than 1 million adults worldwide are believed to have ILDs other than IPF. In addition, up to 50%-60% of non-IPF ILD patients are reported to suffer from an uncontrolled chronic cough. There are no approved therapies for the treatment of non-IPF ILD-related chronic cough. We plan to initiate an
adaptive design Phase 2b clinical trial for the treatment of patients with non-IPF ILD-related chronic cough in the second half of 2026, subject to review of the protocol for the trial by the FDA.

RCC Program. We are developing Haduvio for the treatment of RCC, which affects approximately 2-3 million adults in the U.S. and is related to biological changes in the central and peripheral nervous systems that lower the threshold of the cough reflex. It is highly disruptive and accompanied by a wide range of complications, ranging from urinary incontinence in females to sleep disruption and social embarrassment that causes significant social and economic burden for patients and those around them.

In March 2025, we announced positive topline data from our Phase 2a clinical trial of Haduvio in patients with RCC, which we refer to as the Phase 2a RIVER trial. The Phase 2a RIVER trial was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-treatment, two-period, crossover study that was designed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, tolerability and dosing of Haduvio for the treatment of patients with RCC. The primary endpoint of the trial was the mean change in 24-hour cough frequency, as determined by an objective cough monitor, for the full analysis set population. In the trial, Haduvio met the primary endpoint at Day 21 with a statistically significant reduction in the objective 24-hour cough frequency of 67% from Baseline and 57% from Baseline on a placebo-adjusted basis (p<0.0001). Planned analyses of all pre-specified secondary endpoints, including patient reported endpoints, at the end of treatment were also statistically significant. The safety results of the trial were generally consistent with the known safety profile of Haduvio from previous trials in other patient populations and there were no serious adverse events reported in the trial.

We expect to initiate a Phase 2b trial of Haduvio for the treatment of patients with RCC in the second quarter of 2026, which we are planning to conduct in the United Kingdom, Canada, and possibly other European countries. We expect the primary efficacy endpoint of the trial will be the mean change in 24-hour cough frequency, as determined by an objective cough monitor, and we plan to use the trial to determine the doses to be evaluated in the Phase 3 clinical trial as well as to further characterize safety in this specific patient population. The trial is subject to final review of the protocol by regulatory authorities.

Other NDA Supportive Studies. We also plan to continue to progress and advance NDA supportive studies necessary for regulatory approval, including Phase 1 clinical studies such as completing our respiratory safety study, and conducting drug-drug interaction, food effect, and hepatic and renal impairment studies.
Commercialization of Haduvio. We have retained worldwide commercial rights for Haduvio.

Nalbuphine is a mixed kappa-opioid receptor agonist and a mu-opioid receptor antagonist. The kappa- and mu-opioid receptors are known to be critical mediators of cough. Nalbuphine has been approved and marketed as an injectable for pain indications for decades in the U.S. and Europe. Nalbuphine's mechanism of action also mitigates the risk of abuse associated with mu-opioid agonists because it antagonizes, or blocks, the mu-opioid receptor.

headings: Risks Related to Our Financial Position and Need for Additional Capital
We have incurred significant losses since inception, expect to incur significant and increasing losses for the foreseeable future and may never achieve or maintain profitability.
We have no products approved for commercial sale, which may make it difficult to evaluate the prospects for our future success and viability.
Raising additional capital may cause dilution to our stockholders, restrict our operations or require us to relinquish rights to our product candidates.
Risks Related to the Development and Commercialization of Haduvio and Any Future Product Candidates
Our approach to the development and commercialization of Haduvio to treat chronic cough is unproven.
Clinical drug development involves a lengthy and expensive process with an uncertain outcome.

Our clinical trials may fail to demonstrate adequately the safety and efficacy of Haduvio or any future product candidates, which would likely prevent or delay regulatory approval and commercialization.
Use of patient-reported outcome assessments, or PROs, in our clinical trials and high placebo response rates may delay or impair the development of Haduvio or adversely impact our clinical trials.
If we experience delays or difficulties in the enrollment of patients in clinical trials, our receipt of necessary regulatory approvals could be delayed or prevented.
Results of preclinical studies and clinical trials may not be predictive of results of later clinical trials.
paragraphs: Our business is subject to numerous risks. The following important factors, among others, could cause our actual results to differ materially from those expressed in forward-looking statements made by us or on our behalf in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and other filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, or SEC, press releases, communications with investors, and oral statements. Actual future results may differ materially from those anticipated in our forward-looking statements. We undertake no obligation to update any forward-looking statements, whether as a result of new information, future events, or otherwise.

We have incurred significant annual net losses every year since our inception. We expect to continue to incur significant and increasing net losses for at least the next several years. Our net losses were $42.8 million and $47.9 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $329.8 million. We have not generated any revenues from product sales, have not completed the development of any product candidate and may never have a product candidate approved for commercialization. We have financed our operations to date primarily through private placements of our convertible preferred stock and convertible notes prior to our initial public offering, or IPO, proceeds from our IPO, sales of our common stock and warrants to purchase our common stock, and borrowings from term loans. We have devoted substantially all our financial resources and efforts to the clinical development of our product candidate Haduvio and related activities. Our net losses may fluctuate significantly from quarter to quarter and year to year. Net losses and negative cash flows have had, and will continue to have, an adverse effect on our stockholders' equity and working capital.
We expect to continue to incur significant expenses and increasing operating losses for the foreseeable future. We anticipate that our expenses will increase substantially if and as we:

• continue to develop and conduct clinical trials of Haduvio, including our planned Phase 3 trials of Haduvio for the treatment of chronic cough in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, or IPF, our planned adaptive design Phase 2b clinical trial of Haduvio for the treatment of chronic cough in patients with non-IPF interstitial lung disease, or non-IPF ILD, our planned Phase 2b clinical trial of Haduvio for the treatment of patients with refractory chronic cough, or RCC, and our planned Phase 1 NDA supportive studies;

• complete other development work required for the filing of a new drug application, or NDA, with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, or FDA, and the filing of marketing authorization applications, or MAAs, with the European Medicines Agency, or EMA and the Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency in the United Kingdom, or MHRA, or other government agencies, for Haduvio;

• seek regulatory and marketing approvals for Haduvio for the treatment of chronic cough in patients with IPF, non-IPF ILD or RCC or for any future product candidate that successfully completes clinical trials, if any;

paragraphs: 本公司為一家臨牀階段生技藥品公司，專注於開發與商業化臨牀試驗藥物Haduvio（口服 nalbuphine ER）用以治療因特發性肺纖維化（IPF）、非IPF間質性肺病（非IPF ILD）及難治性慢性咳嗽（RCC）所引起的慢性咳嗽。

Haduvio為口服延效型 nalbuphine 製劑。Haduvio透過作用於咳嗽反射弧的中樞與週邊途徑，作為kappa受體活化劑與mu受體拮抗劑（"KAMA"），針對在控制慢性咳嗽中扮演關鍵角色的阿片受體。kappa與mu阿片受體被認為是咳嗽的重要媒介。Nalbuphine已獲美國（U.S.）與歐洲批准並上市銷售作為疼痛治療用途多年。Nalbuphine的作用機制亦可降低與mu阿片活化劑相關的濫用風險，因其會拮抗（阻斷）mu阿片受體。注射用 nalbuphine 在美國藥物濫用管理局（DEA）未被列為管制藥物，且在大多數歐洲國家亦非管制藥物。本公司認為這使 Haduvio 成為治療 IPF、非IPF ILD 及 RCC 患者慢性咳嗽的潛在優良療法。

IPF相關慢性咳嗽計畫。本公司正在開發 Haduvio 用以治療 IPF 相關慢性咳嗽，這是一種進行性纖維化間質性肺病，與高死亡率相關。在診斷為 IPF 後，患者的中位生存期為 3 至 5 年，此期間患者會經歷慢性咳嗽、呼吸困難與疲勞。IPF 相關慢性咳嗽是一種未被滿足的醫療需求，且美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）尚未核准任何治療此症的藥物。美國約有 150,000 名 IPF 患者，其中三分之二的患者有未受控制的慢性咳嗽。慢性咳嗽的影響極大，患者每日咳嗽次數可達 1,500 次。這種持續性的咳嗽，以及任何相關的損傷，可能會導致更高的癮病與死亡風險，包括疾病惡化、更高的疾病進展風險、增加的呼吸道住院次數，以及患者生理、心理與社會生活品質的下降。

2025 年 6 月，本公司宣佈 Phase 2b CORAL 研究的初步結果為正面，該研究為一劑量範圍研究，評估 Haduvio 對 IPF 相關慢性咳嗽的療效、安全性與耐受性。Phase 2b CORAL 研究為一隨機、雙盲、安慰劑對照、平行組設計，評估三種不同劑量組的 Haduvio（108 mg BID、54 mg BID 與 27 mg BID）與安慰劑的比較。該研究的主要療效終點為修改後的意向治療羣（modified intent-to-treat，或 mITT 羣）在第 6 週末與基線相比的 24 小時咳嗽頻率（每小時咳嗽次數）相對變化，透過客觀咳嗽監測器進行測量。mITT 羣包含所有隨機化患者，且至少接受一劑研究藥物或安慰劑（n=165）。Phase 2b CORAL 研究的主要療效終點已達成，顯示在第 6 週，所有劑量組的 24 小時咳嗽頻率均有統計學顯著的減少。108 mg BID、54 mg BID 與 27 mg BID 劑量組相較於安慰劑，基線值的減少分別為 60.2%（p<0.0001）、53.4%（p<0.0001）與 47.9%（p<0.01），而安慰劑組的基線值減少為 16.9%。

本公司已完成與 FDA 的 Phase 2 結束會議。在會議中，我們獲得對未來臨牀試驗計畫的總體一致意見，以支持 nalbuphine ER 的新藥申請（NDA）提交，包括兩項關鍵的 Phase 3 臨牀試驗，以及對剩餘 Phase 1 臨牀試驗的同意。Phase 3 試驗將同時進行，本公司預計在 2026 年第二季啟動第一項 Phase 3 試驗，並在 2026 年第二季後半啟動第二項 Phase 3 試驗。第一項 Phase 3 試驗預計招募約 300 名患者，進行 52 週的固定劑量 nalbuphine ER 54 mg 早晚各一次（BID）治療，主要終點為 24 週固定劑量治療後的變化。第二項 Phase 3 試驗預計招募約 130 名患者，進行 12 週的固定劑量 nalbuphine ER 54 mg BID 治療。兩項試驗的主要療效終點為 nalbuphine ER 與安慰劑相比，24 小時咳嗽頻率（每小時咳嗽次數）的相對變化，透過客觀咳嗽監測器測量。這些試驗設計將接受 FDA 對試驗計畫的最終審查。
非IPF ILD相關慢性咳嗽計畫。本公司也計畫開發 Haduvio 用以治療非IPF ILD 相關的慢性咳嗽。許多被診斷為非IPF ILD 的患者會經歷乾咳、非產性慢性咳嗽，其幹擾程度與 IPF 相關的咳嗽相當。咳嗽可能為非IPF ILD 患者疾病惡化的獨立預測因子，因此本公司認為慢性咳嗽可能促進基礎疾病的進展與惡化健康結果。

美國約有 228,000 名成人及全球超過 1,000,000 名成人被認為患有非 IPF 的 ILD。此外，據報導，約有 50%-60% 的非 IPF ILD 患者會經歷未受控制的慢性咳嗽。目前尚無核准用以治療非 IPF ILD 相關慢性咳嗽的療法。本公司計畫在 2026 年第二季後半，針對非 IPF ILD 相關慢性咳嗽患者啟動一項適應性設計的 Phase 2b 臨牀試驗，前提是該試驗計畫經 FDA 審查批准。
adaptive design Phase 2b 臨牀試驗計畫於 2026 年第二季後半啟動，前提是該試驗計畫經 FDA 審查批准。
RCC 程式。我們正在開發 Haduvio 用於治療 RCC，此症狀影響美國約 2-3 百萬成年人，與影響中樞及週邊神經系統的生物變化有關，這些變化會降低咳嗽反射的門檻。此症狀高度幹擾且伴隨廣泛的併發症，從女性泌尿失禁到睡眠幹擾及社會尷尬，會對患者及其周遭的人造成顯著的社會與經濟負擔。

2025 年 3 月，我們宣佈在 RCC 患者中進行 Haduvio 的 Phase 2a 臨牀試驗結果為正面，我們稱此為 Phase 2a RIVER 試驗。Phase 2a RIVER 試驗是一項隨機、雙盲、安慰劑對照、兩治療組、兩期交叉試驗，設計用以評估 Haduvio 對治療 RCC 患者的有效性、安全性、耐受性及劑量。試驗的主要終點為 24 小時咳嗽頻率的平均變化，以客觀咳嗽監測器所確定的結果，針對完整分析集人口。在試驗中，Haduvio 在第 21 天達成主要終點，以客觀 24 小時咳嗽頻率為基準，與基線相比統計顯著減少 67%，在安慰劑調整基準下與基線相比減少 57%（p<0.0001）。預計在治療結束時，所有預先指定的次要終點，包括患者報告終點，也均顯示統計顯著。試驗的安全性結果與 Haduvio 在其他患者族羣中先前試驗所知的安全性資料大致一致，且試驗中未報告嚴重不良事件。

我們預期在 2026 年第二季啟動 Haduvio 對治療 RCC 患者的 Phase 2b 試驗，我們計畫在英國、加拿大及其他可能的歐洲國家進行。我們預期試驗的主要有效性終點為 24 小時咳嗽頻率的平均變化，以客觀咳嗽監測器所確定的結果，並計畫使用此試驗以確定 Phase 3 臨牀試驗中將評估的劑量，以及進一步_characterize_此特定患者族羣的安全性。此試驗需經監管當局對試驗計畫的最終審查。
其他 NDA 支持性研究。我們也計畫持續進行及推進 NDA 支持性研究，以符合監管核准，包括 Phase 1 臨牀研究，例如完成我們的呼吸安全性研究，以及進行藥物間交互作用、食物影響、以及肝臟與腎臟功能障礙研究。
Haduvio 的商業化。我們已保留 Haduvio 全球商業權。
Nalbuphine 是一種混合 kappa-阿片受體激動劑及 mu-阿片受體拮抗劑。kappa- 和 mu- 阿片受體被認為是咳嗽的關鍵中介物。Nalbuphine 已經獲准並上市作為注射劑用於疼痛治療，已持續在美國和歐洲使用多年。Nalbuphine 的作用機制也降低與 mu- 阿片激動劑相關的濫用風險，因為它拮抗，或阻斷，mu- 阿片受體。

我們是一家臨牀階段的生物製藥公司，專注於開發與商業化正在研究中的療法Haduvio（口服nalbuphine ER）用於治療患有特發性肺纖維化（IPF）、非IPF間質性肺病（非IPF ILD）或難治性慢性咳嗽（RCC）患者的慢性咳嗽。Haduvio是一種口服延長釋放型的nalbuphine。Haduvio透過作用於咳嗽反射弧，同時在中樞與週邊作用，作為kappa受體活化劑與mu受體拮抗劑（"KAMA"），針對在控制慢性咳嗽中扮演關鍵角色的阿片受體。kappa與mu阿片受體被認為是咳嗽的關鍵中介物。Nalbuphine已獲批准並作為注射劑用於疼痛治療數十年，在美國（U.S.）與歐洲。Nalbuphine的作用機制也減少了與mu阿片活化劑相關的濫用風險，因為它拮抗，或阻斷，mu阿片受體。靜脈注射nalbuphine未被美國藥物濫用管理局（DEA）列為管制藥物，在大多數歐洲國家亦然。
與IPF相關的慢性咳嗽計畫。我們正在開發Haduvio用於治療與IPF相關的慢性咳嗽，這是一種進行性纖維化間質性肺病，與高死亡率相關。

2025年6月，我們宣佈在Phase 2b CORAL試驗中取得正面的初步結果，這是一項劑量範圍研究，評估Haduvio對IPF相關慢性咳嗽的療效、安全性與耐受性。Phase 2b CORAL試驗是一項隨機、雙盲、安慰劑對照、平行組設計，評估三種不同劑量組的Haduvio（108 mg BID、54 mg BID與27 mg BID）與安慰劑的比較。試驗的主要療效終點為修改後的意向治療（mITT）族羣在第6週末與基線相比的24小時咳嗽頻率（每小時咳嗽次數）的相對變化，透過客觀咳嗽監測器測量。mITT族羣包含所有隨機化患者，至少接受一劑試驗藥物或安慰劑（n=165）。Phase 2b CORAL試驗的主要療效終點已達成，顯示在第6週，所有劑量組的24小時咳嗽頻率均有統計學顯著的減少。108 mg BID、54 mg BID與27 mg BID劑量組分別從基線減少60.2%（p<0.0001）、53.4%（p<0.0001）與47.9%（p<0.01），與安慰劑組從基線減少16.9%相比。

我們已完成與FDA的Phase 2期末會議。在會議中，我們達成對未來臨牀研究計畫的總體協議，以支持nalbuphine ER的NDA申請，包括兩項關鍵的Phase 3臨牀試驗，並達成對剩餘Phase 1臨牀試驗的協議。Phase 3試驗將同時進行，我們預計在2026年第二季啟動第一項Phase 3試驗，並在2026年下半年啟動第二項Phase 3試驗。第一項Phase 3試驗計畫招募約300名患者，進行52週的固定劑量nalbuphine ER 54 mg BID，主要終點為24週的固定劑量。第二項Phase 3試驗計畫招募約130名患者，進行12週的固定劑量nalbuphine ER 54 mg BID。兩項試驗的主要療效終點為nalbuphine ER與安慰劑相比，24小時咳嗽頻率（每小時咳嗽次數）從基線的相對變化，透過客觀咳嗽監測器測定。這些試驗設計將接受FDA對試驗方案的最終審查。
與非IPF ILD相關的慢性咳嗽計畫。我們也計畫開發Haduvio用於治療與非IPF ILD相關的慢性咳嗽。我們計畫在2026年下半年啟動一項適應性設計的Phase 2b臨牀試驗，用於治療患有與非IPF ILD相關的慢性咳嗽的患者，前提是試驗方案經FDA審查批准。
RCC 程式。我們正在開發 Haduvio 用於治療 RCC，此症狀影響美國約 2-3 百萬成人，與中樞及周邊神經系統的生物學變化有關，這些變化會降低咳嗽反射的門檻。此症狀極具幹擾性，並伴隨廣泛的併發症，從女性的尿失禁到睡眠中斷以及社會尷尬，會對患者及其周遭的人造成顯著的社會與經濟負擔。

2025 年 3 月，我們宣佈 Haduvio 在治療 RCC 患者之 Phase 2a 臨牀試驗結果為正面，我們稱此為 Phase 2a RIVER 試驗。Phase 2a RIVER 試驗為一隨機、雙盲、安慰劑對照、兩治療組、兩期交叉試驗，設計用以評估 Haduvio 在治療 RCC 患者時的療效、安全性、耐受性及劑量。試驗的主要終點為 24 小時咳嗽頻率的平均變化，由客觀咳嗽監測器所測定，針對完整分析集人口。在試驗中，Haduvio 在第 21 天達成主要終點，以客觀 24 小時咳嗽頻率為基準，與基線相比顯著減少 67%，與安慰劑調整基準相比減少 57%（p<0.0001）。預計在治療結束時，所有預先指定的次要終點，包括患者報告終點，也均顯示統計學顯著性。試驗的安全性結果與 Haduvio 在其他患者羣體中已知的安全性資料一致，且試驗中未報告嚴重不良事件。
我們預期在 2026 年第二季啟動 Haduvio 用於治療 RCC 患者的 Phase 2b 試驗，計畫在英國、加拿大及可能的其他歐洲國家進行。此試驗需經監管當局對試驗計畫進行最終審查。
其他 NDA 支持性研究。我們也計畫持續進行及推進 NDA 支持性研究，以取得監管批准，包括 Phase 1 臨牀研究，例如完成我們的呼吸安全性研究，以及進行藥物間交互作用、食物影響、以及肝臟及腎臟功能障礙研究。

自 2011 年開始營運以來，我們已將 substantially all 的努力與財務資源投入 Haduvio 的臨牀開發。我們尚未從產品銷售中產生任何收入，因此我們從未獲利，且自營運開始以來每年均產生淨虧損。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們累積虧損為 329.8 百萬美元，主要為研究與開發費用及一般及行政費用所致。我們不預期會產生產品收入，除非且僅在取得 Haduvio 用於治療慢性咳嗽的 IPF、非 IPF ILD 或 RCC 患者之行銷批准並進行商業化後。我們無法保證我們將產生顯著的收入或利潤。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們持有現金、現金等價物及市場可交易證券為 188.3 百萬美元。我們認為現有的現金、現金等價物及市場可交易證券足以支持我們至少 12 個月的營運費用及資本支出需求，自本年度報表（包含於本 10-K 年度報告中）發佈日算起。

headings: 與本公司財務狀況相關的風險及對額外資金的需求

與Haduvio及任何未來產品候選藥物的開發與商業化相關的風險
本公司針對以Haduvio治療慢性咳嗽的開發與商業化方法尚未經驗證。
臨牀藥物開發涉及漫長且昂貴的過程，且結果具有不確定性。
本公司臨牀試驗可能無法充分顯示Haduvio或任何未來產品候選藥物的安全性與有效性，這將可能導致或延遲監管批准與商業化。
於我們的臨牀試驗中使用病患自述結果評估，或 PROs，以及高安慰劑反應率，可能會延誤或影響 Haduvio 的開發，並對我們的臨牀試驗產生不利影響。
若我們在臨牀試驗中遭遇患者入組的延誤或困難，我們取得必要的監管核准可能會被延誤或無法取得。
預臨牀研究及臨牀試驗的結果可能無法預測後續臨牀試驗的結果。
paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨許多風險。以下重要因素，及其他因素，可能會導致本公司實際結果與我們或代表本公司在本年度報告表 10-K 及其他向證券交易委員會，或 SEC，提交的文件、新聞稿、與投資者溝通及口頭陳述中所發表的預測性陳述有重大差異。實際未來結果可能與我們預測性陳述中所預期的有重大差異。本公司不負有任何更新預測性陳述的義務，無論是因新資訊、未來事件或其他原因。

自本公司成立以來，我們每年均產生顯著的淨虧損。我們預期將持續產生顯著且不斷增加的淨虧損，至少在未來數年內。本公司於 2025 年 12 月 31 日結算年度的淨虧損為 42.8 百萬美元，2024 年 12 月 31 日結算年度的淨虧損為 47.9 百萬美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司累計虧損為 329.8 百萬美元。本公司尚未從產品銷售中產生任何收入，也尚未完成任何產品候選品的開發，且可能永遠不會有產品候選品獲得商業化批准。本公司至今主要透過私募發行可轉換優先股與可轉換票據、首次公開發行股票，或 IPO 的所得、股票與認購權證的銷售，以及取得期貨貸款來資助營運。本公司已將幾乎所有財務資源與努力投入產品候選品 Haduvio 的臨牀開發及相關活動。本公司淨虧損可能在每季與每年之間有顯著波動。淨虧損與負面現金流已對本公司股東權益與營運資金產生，且將持續產生負面影響。
我們預期將持續產生顯著費用與增加的營運虧損，至少在可預見的未來。我們預期，如果我們：

• 繼續開發與進行 Haduvio 的臨牀試驗，包括我們計畫的 Haduvio 對於患有特發性肺纖維化，或 IPF 患者慢性咳嗽的第三期試驗、我們計畫的 Haduvio 對於患有非 IPF 間質性肺病，或非 IPF ILD 患者慢性咳嗽的適應性設計第二期 b 階段臨牀試驗、我們計畫的 Haduvio 對於患有難治性慢性咳嗽，或 RCC 患者的第二期 b 階段臨牀試驗，以及我們計畫的 Haduvio 的新藥申請，或 NDA 支持性第一期研究；
• 完成其他為提交新藥申請，或 NDA 給美國食品藥物管理局，或 FDA，以及提交市場許可申請，或 MAAs 給歐洲藥物管理局，或 EMA 和英國藥物與醫療產品監管局，或 MHRA，或其他政府機構所需的開發工作，以 Haduvio 為對象；
• 尋求 Haduvio 對於患有 IPF、非 IPF ILD 或 RCC 的慢性咳嗽治療的監管與市場許可批准，或對於任何成功完成臨牀試驗的未來產品候選品的批准，如果有的話；
